title: Control Plane sprint 62 check-in: routing/auth/quotas deep-dive
content:
Date: 2026-06-09
Sprint: 62 
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Sofia, Liam, Jun, Priya (ops)
Length: 40m (quick sync + two focused dive segments)

Purpose: Weekly check-in focused on three cross-cutting control plane concerns we keep seeing in customer reports — routing fallbacks, auth token churn, and soft quota enforcement. Goal: surface new risks, agree immediate mitigations, and capture action owners + lifespans.

1) Quick status + small wins (5m)
- Canary rollout for route-fallback logic to tier-2 models completed on 2026-06-07; initial metrics show 12% reduction in 5xx during sustained load tests. (Marco)
- New unit tests for multi-tenant policy resolution merged to main (PR #4182) — helps reproduce earlier race that caused incorrect tenant routing. (Sofia)
- Quotas dashboard now shows per-route soft-limit vs. hard-limit band; UX follow-up scheduled with Console PM. (Jun)

2) Routing deep-dive (12m)
Notes: Recent incidents show routing policy evaluation sometimes falls back to regional default even when local capacity exists. Hypothesis: stale capacity cache combined with async capacity updates from Dedicated pools.
- Repro steps: simulate rapid Dedicated pool scale-up -> capacity cache not invalidated for ~9s -> router picks fallback variant.
- Impact: intermittent increased latency (p50 unaffected, p95 increases by ~70–120ms) and occasional content mismatch when fallback is a different quantization profile.
- Short-term mitigation: reduce cache TTL for capacity metadata from 10s -> 3s for tiered routes. Rollout window: next 48h, rate-limited to 10% of nodes (Marco).
- Longer-term: introduce per-pool change stream (webhook/event) to invalidate cache immediate on scale events; tracked in PLT-2978.
- Open question: whether 3s TTL will cause extra control plane load during high churn — need synthetic load test. (Action: Marco + SRE to run test by 2026-06-12)

3) Auth/token churn and agent reconnects (10m)
Notes: A handful of enterprise customers reported short-lived 401s when tokens rotated during a burst of requests; client SDKs retried but saw elevated error budget utilization.
- Root cause: token rotation path held a micro-window where cached session state referenced old signing key; local SDK caches did not prefetch refreshed tokens.
- Immediate fix: add grace acceptance for tokens signed with last-known key for 30s; update edge auth proxy to accept both keys temporarily. (Sofia)
- SDK change: prefetch + backoff jitter on 401 to avoid stampeding refreshes. Prepare patch for JS & Python SDKs. (Action: Sofia -> patch by 2026-06-14)
- Monitoring: add a 401 spike alert scoped to token_rotation label. (Priya)

4) Quotas: soft enforcement, throttling policy, and customer messaging (8m)
Notes: Confusion in support tickets about soft vs hard quotas — customers hit soft-limit and saw degraded throughput rather than clear messaging.
- Proposal: wire smart-throttling where soft-limit causes 429 with Retry-After and helpful header X-Quota-Detail. Hard-limit remains 403. UX copy drafted in product ticket.
- Experiments: A/B test messaging with two pilot accounts next week. (Jun to coordinate)
- Infra: need a small change in API gateway to attach detailed headers; low-risk, deployable in canary. (Action: Liam to deliver gateway patch by 2026-06-16)

5) Incidents / small postmortem notes (3m)
- 2026-06-03: brief routing fallback spike during internal perf test — mitigations done; incident write-up will go to Confluence. Postmortem owner: Marco (due 2026-06-13).

6) Action items and owners (concise)
- Marco + SRE: synthetic load test for 3s TTL plan; due 2026-06-12.
- Marco: rollout capacity TTL reduction to 10% nodes; monitor 5xx and latency; start 2026-06-10.
- Sofia: SDK prefetch + jitter patch (JS/Python); due 2026-06-14.
- Sofia + Ops (Priya): 401-spike alert and dashboard tile; due 2026-06-12.
- Liam: gateway header change for smart-quota; PR + canary deploy by 2026-06-16.
- Jun: coordinate UX A/B pilot for quota messaging; identify pilot accounts by 2026-06-11.
- Marco: incident postmortem draft for 2026-06-03 event; due 2026-06-13.

7) Risks & decisions (2m)
- Decision: accept 3s TTL risk for next 72 hours while running synthetic tests. If CPU/control-plane load increases > 15% we will rollback.
- Risk: SDK staggered updates means some client versions will still be exposed to token churn for ~4 weeks. Escalate to Customer Success for targeted outreach. (Aisha)

8) Misc notes / open threads (freeform)
- Evaluate whether we can tag tenant-level route policies with a criticality score so fallback policy is informed by content parity (important for customers using quantization-sensitive models).
- Consider a small feature flag to allow chosen customers to opt-out of automatic fallback to lower-quality quant variants. (Product ask)
- Follow-up meeting: dedicated routing architecture review (invite infra + serving-runtime) scheduled for 2026-06-15, 11:00 PT.

Next check-in: 2026-06-16 (same channel)

Marked for visibility: please add any missing context or objections in-thread. If you pick up an action, add your name to the ticket and ping me.

Raw notes / shorthand (copied from whiteboard):
- TTL 10s -> 3s (tiered routes), canary 10% nodes, metric to watch: 'route.fallback.rate' & 'controlplane.cpu'
- Auth: accept previous signing key for 30s; SDK prefetch + jitter; alert: auth.401.spike(token_rotation:true)
- Quotas: 429+Retry-After + header X-Quota-Detail, pilot 2 accounts, timeline 1 week

----
